content: 1. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels or effects of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Close monitoring is recommended, and caution should be exercised. 2. Drugs that alter the pH of the upper gastrointestinal (GI) tract, such as proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), H2-blockers, and antacids, may decrease the solubility and bioavailability of dabrafenib. Alternative therapies should be considered in serious cases. 3. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of dapsone by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 4. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of dasatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 5. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of deferasirox. Although deferasirox has a lower affinity for aluminum than for iron, it should not be administered with aluminum-containing antacid preparations. Avoid this combination and monitor closely. 6. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of deferiprone by enhancing GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 7. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of deferiprone by enhancing GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Deferiprone may bind to polyvalent cations (e.g., iron, aluminum, zinc); administration should be separated by at least 4 hours between deferiprone and other medications or supplements containing these cations. 8. Deferoxamine decreases the levels of aluminum hydroxide by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Deferoxamine chelates iron, but its affinity for other minerals is unknown. 9. Magnesium hydroxide and deflazacort both decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 10. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of delafloxacin by cation binding in the GI tract. Oral delafloxacin forms chelates with alkaline earth and transition metal cations. Administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these agents. In serious cases, alternative therapies should be used. 11. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of demeclocycline by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 12. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of demeclocycline by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 13. Devil’s claw decreases the effects of aluminum hydroxide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 14. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels or effects of dextroamphetamine by passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 15. Dextrose increases the renal clearance of magnesium hydroxide, thereby decreasing its levels. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 16. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels or effects of digoxin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 17. Digoxin decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 18. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of dolutegravir by cation binding in the GI tract. Administer dolutegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after taking medications containing polyvalent cations. Use alternative therapy if available. 19. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of dolutegravir by cation binding in the GI tract. Administer dolutegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after taking medications containing polyvalent cations. Use alternative therapy if available. 20. Doxercalciferol increases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by enhancing GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown.
